title: The Odyssey
subtitle: The Long Way Home
attribution: An original abridged adaptation of Homer’s Odyssey
intro: A door left open. A name that should have stayed hidden.
ending: He had escaped the cave. He had given the sea a name to follow.
description: Odysseus remembers the lotus, the cave and the moment pride undid his cleverest escape.

adaptationSource.note: Original abridged dialogue and narration. Ismarus is condensed into aftermath; one invented companion, Doros, represents the losses in the cave. The attack is implied without graphic imagery. Eurylochus represents the surviving crew. The lotus and escape are condensed.

steps.text: Odysseus was telling his story in Alcinous’s hall. In his memory, the war at Troy had just ended, and his crew was still alive.
“I thought leaving the war behind would be enough.”
Before this departure, they had attacked a town for supplies. Its people fought back. Some of his sailors died.
Doros, one of the sailors who had fought beside Odysseus, stood with him. Eurylochus was another of his companions.
“The ship is ready.”
They climbed aboard. One more departure, and still no homecoming.

transition.reason: The departure establishes open water with the complete ship and crew

steps.text: The wind carried them off their course. Days passed before they found a quiet place to land.
Another shore lay ahead. It would offer something sweeter than hope.

islander.zone: Right edge of the lotus path

steps.text: The islander held out a lotus blossom. There was no weapon in her hands, no demand in her voice.
“You look tired. Stay a little.”
Doros tasted it. His shoulders loosened. The hurry went out of him.
“We should go,” Odysseus said. “The others are waiting.”
“Let them wait. What is there to hurry toward?”
The lotus made Doros forget why he wanted to go home. He wanted to stay here instead of returning to Ithaca.
Odysseus took his arm and brought him back toward the ship, though Doros begged to stay.
“You can be angry with me on the way home.”

transition.reason: The complete crew sails away from the lotus island

steps.text: He had saved his companion from forgetting. On the next shore, he would forget to listen.

steps.text: After landing and walking into the cave, they found baskets of cheese. They decided to wait for the shepherd who lived here.
“Take what we need and go. We should not wait for him.”
“Perhaps he will offer us shelter. I want to meet him.”
The shepherd was Polyphemus, a giant with one eye. He rolled a huge stone across the entrance, trapping the men inside.
“We are travelers. We ask for the kindness owed to guests.”
“You speak as if your customs rule my cave.”
The giant killed Doros. The men who remained drew together. This was no shelter.
Even if they killed him, they could not move that stone. They needed him alive to open the way.
Odysseus had brought wine ashore. Now it was the beginning of a desperate plan.
Polyphemus drank the strong wine. The cup looked small in his hand.
“More. And tell me your name.”
“Nobody. That is what they call me.”
“Then Nobody will be the last of his companions I eat.”
At last, the wine brought sleep. Odysseus lifted the sharpened olive stake. Eurylochus kept watch.
They struck his single eye and drew back. Blinded, Polyphemus called to the Cyclopes outside.
“Nobody is hurting me!”
The other giants thought he meant that no person was attacking him. Odysseus’s false name had fooled them, so they did not help.
The name had bought them time. It had not moved the stone.
Beside them, the rams waited for morning. Odysseus watched their heavy wool.
At dawn, Polyphemus moved the stone to let his flock out. The men clung beneath the rams.
He felt along the animals’ backs. The wool above them passed beneath his hand.

transition.reason: From the cave to the open coast

steps.text: Outside, they let go of the wool. The ship was still waiting.

steps.text: They sailed clear. It should have been enough to be alive.
“Keep your voice down. Let him lose us.”
But Odysseus turned toward the shore. Nobody was a name he could no longer bear.
“It was Odysseus who escaped you! Son of Laertes, from Ithaca!”

steps.text: Polyphemus prayed to his father, Poseidon, the god of the sea. Because Odysseus had shouted his real name, the giant could name him.
“If he must reach home, let him reach it late, alone, and in another man’s ship.”

steps.text: Odysseus had escaped, but Poseidon heard his son’s prayer. The angry sea god would make his journey home harder.
